# FDGA048

> DO use the `nameof(...)` syntax, instead of a literal string, when referring to the name of a type, member, or parameter.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section A.1.6 Other.

This is a coding style convention. The book treats the appendix A conventions as suggestions, so you can override it.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1507
- Automatic fix: yes
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Language: [C# 6+] (before that: Before C# 6, use a string literal that matches the name exactly.)
- Status: verified

CA1507 reports string literals that match a parameter or property name.

## From the book

```csharp
Right: throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(target));
Wrong: throw new ArgumentNullException("target");
```
